Styling Plotly Figures in R

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/styling-figures.Rmd
styling-figures.Rmd

Styling Figures made with Plotly

Plotly’s R graphing library makes it easy to create interactive, publication-quality graphs.

More specifically, here are the 2 ways you can style and customize figures made with plotly.core:

  1. Control common parameters like titles, labeling and colors with the arguments of the add_<trace>() functions
  2. Updating the figure’s layout with update_layout(), update_xaxes(), update_yaxes() and friends

Built-in Plotly Styling Arguments

Many common styling options can be set directly when adding traces and updating the layout:

  • title (in update_layout()) to set the figure title
  • name to set the legend entry of each trace, and title in go_xaxis(), go_yaxis() and go_legend() to set axis and legend titles. By default, axes are titled with the column names in the x and y formulas.
  • categoryorder and categoryarray in go_xaxis() to override the default category ordering behaviour, which is to use the levels of a factor, or otherwise the order in which the data appears in the input.
  • hovertemplate, hoverinfo and the axes’ hoverformat to control which attributes appear in the hover label and how they are formatted.
  • Various color-related attributes such as marker = go_bar_marker(color = ...), colorscale, colorbar and the layout colorway set the colors used in the figure.

To illustrate each of these, here is a simple, default figure made with Plotly, with one bar trace per payer gender. Note the default orderings for the x-axis categories.

library(reshape2)
library(plotly.core)

data("tips")

tips |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_bar(x = ~day, y = ~total_bill, split = ~sex) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "stack")

Here is the same figure, restyled by adding some extra parameters:

library(reshape2)
library(plotly.core)

data("tips")

sex_colors <- c(Female = "#3399FF", Male = "#FF6666")

xform <- go_xaxis(
  title = "Day of Week",
  categoryorder = "array",
  categoryarray = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
)

tips |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = sex_colors) |>
  add_bar(
    x = ~day,
    y = ~total_bill,
    marker = go_bar_marker(color = ~sex)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    barmode = "stack",
    xaxis = xform,
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Sum of Receipts"),
    title = "Receipts by Payer Gender and Day of Week",
    legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "<b> Payer Gender </b>"))
  )

Updating or Modifying Figures made with Plotly

Here is the same figure as above, with some additional customizations to the axes and legend.

library(reshape2)
library(plotly.core)

data("tips")

sex_colors <- c(Female = "#3399FF", Male = "#FF6666")

xform <- go_xaxis(
  title = "Day of Week",
  categoryorder = "array",
  categoryarray = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
)

fig <- tips |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = sex_colors) |>
  add_bar(
    x = ~day,
    y = ~total_bill,
    marker = go_bar_marker(color = ~sex)
  )
# the y-axis prefix given as dollars
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    barmode = "stack",
    xaxis = xform,
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Sum of Receipts", tickprefix = "$"),
    title = "Receipts by Payer Gender and Day of Week"
  )
# customize legend orientation & position
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(legend = go_legend(x = 0.2, y = 1, orientation = "h"))
# add a horizontal "target" line
fig <- fig |>
  add_shape(
    type = "line",
    xref = "paper",
    x0 = 0,
    x1 = 1,
    y0 = 950,
    y1 = 950,
    line = go_shape_line(dash = "dash", color = "black")
  )
# add a text callout with arrow
fig <- fig |>
  add_annotation(
    x = "Fri",
    y = 400,
    text = "Below Target !",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 1,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  )
# customize font
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(font = go_font(family = "Rockwell"))

fig
